install_opencode_runtime.py is invoked from the Railway [build] buildCommand (deploy build time), not from a preDeploy bootstrap, so it never mounts or accesses the /data volume; it writes only the pinned binary under /app/bin. The idempotent volume-aware startup seam (railway_issuer_startup.py) and its signing-key scrub are untouched.

findings.evidence: Runtime-integrity gate: the installer must refuse to install anything but the exact pinned archive. Verified: _download() verifies the SHA-256 after streaming and raises OpenCodeInstallError on mismatch; _verify_platform() and single-member extraction fail closed; main() returns 2 and installs nothing on any failure, so a tampered or unreachable release aborts the build rather than starting with an untrusted binary.

Atomic, standalone installation: the extracted binary must not be partially installed or left executable mid-write. Verified: extraction writes only the single `opencode` regular member to a .tmp sibling then os.replace(); chmod 0o755 is applied before replace, and no archive path is ever traversed (only the matched member is read), so no foreign artifact or partial binary survives.

Runtime discoverability of the installed binary is an operator wiring concern surfaced by the hostile pass. The governed adapter resolves the OpenCode executable via HUNTER_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE (default "opencode") through PATH lookup; the installer installs to /app/bin/opencode. If the RAILPACK runtime PATH does not include /app/bin and the operator does not set HUNTER_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE=/app/bin/opencode, the first OpenCode dispatch will fail closed with 'OpenCode executable is unavailable'. Fail-closed, so this is not unsafe, but the runbook must document the provisioning step before the first OpenCode dispatch.

The download in _download() streams the archive without a content-length cap before verifying SHA-256. Because the URL is a pinned immutable GitHub release and the digest is verified before any install, the worst case is bounded build-time disk usage; a size cap or redirect policy check is suggested hardening, not a current safety defect.

Tests cover single-member extraction success, fail-closed behavior for a missing/unexpected member, and the immutability/checksum-pin invariants over the pinned constants (v1.18.30, 64-hex SHA-256). The network download path and the platform gate are not unit-tested because they are OS/network dependent; the tested extraction contract exercises the same OpenCodeInstallError fail-closed path as the download gate.
